notes:
Summary: Matrixline is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a customer-facing conversational assistant + internal reranking/embedding pipelines. They emphasize low tail latency for chat at peak traffic and strict data residency/VPC controls. Team is risk-averse on model drift and wants Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization.

Workshop findings (big bullets, shorthand):
- Workload mix: chat (~60% traffic), reranking (20%), embeddings (20%).
- Steady-state baseline QPS: 12 QPS (observed weekdays 09:00-17:00 for sample cohort).
- Average tokens per response: 180-260 (median ~220 tokens).
- Baseline token/sec target: ~2.6k token/sec (220 tokens * 12 QPS).
- Peak multiplier observed: 8-10x (marketing pushes + nightly batch triggers). Planning peak QPS ~= 120.
- Peak token/sec: ~26k token/sec at sustained peak windows (short bursts 2-5 min).
- Latency SLO asks: p95 end-to-end response < 450ms; p99 < 900ms for chat (including first-token and finalization).
- Throughput guarantees requested: sustained baseline with headroom for 10x short bursts; want predictable token/sec pricing for budget modeling.
- Preferred models: open-model variants (L2-like 70B family) quantized to int8/int4 for cost, but want Redwood to hold validated model variants for fallback.
- Quantization / performance: Matrixline prefers Redwood to recommend quantization profile (Optimize) and run microbenchmarks during POC.
- Caching: strong interest in prefix/KV cache for conversational sessions (80% session reuse behavior).
- Routing: plan to route high-cost use to cheaper quantized variants; require policy-based routing by route and customer tier.

Capacity planning decisions from workshop: advanced notes
- Baseline reservation approach: reserve capacity for steady-state + 25% headroom. Recommendation from SE: reserve 8 x H100-class nodes (primary pool) to cover baseline steady-state at target SLOs with quantized model and continuous batching.
- Burst/elastic pool: add autoscale pool of 4-8 additional nodes to handle peaks; prefer burst to be billed separately vs overcommit credits.
- Rationale: 1 H100-class node estimated to sustain ~12-15 QPS for their configured model & batching window; numbers will be validated in POC. Reserve to cover typical daytime load, burst pool for marketing spikes.
- Token budget: estimated monthly token volume ~1.6B-2.4B tokens (depends on peak frequency). Finance flagged tokens cost sensitivity; asked for a model-level cost breakdown in pricing deck.

SLA negotiation points (account wants these in contract):
- Uptime: 99.9% for Dedicated control and inference plane; credits for breach.
- Latency SLOs: Redwood to provide p95/p99 latency pacts for declared model+node configuration; include rollback policies for model rollouts.
- Capacity guarantees: minimum throughput per reserved GPU pool; Redwood to commit to capacity handoff (region fallback) if capacity constrained.
- Data controls: VPC-only management plane, customer-managed KMS, audit log retention 12 months (negotiable).

Open risks / blockers:
- Procurement timeline: legal needs standard MSA + SOC2 addendum (expected 4-6 weeks).
- Security ATO: SecOps needs successful review of encryption in transit + at rest, and verification of audit log export.
- Network: VPC peering and egress policy tests required; infra team needs specific IP ranges and route tables from Redwood.
- Cost sensitivity: matrixline finance wants a blended per-token + reserved-node break even at 12 QPS baseline; will compare to AWS-hosted alternatives.

POC scope (agreed):
- 2-week dedicated POC: 4 reserved H100 nodes + 2 burst nodes, run customer traffic replay (anonymized traces) against chosen quantized model.
- Deliverables: bench report (QPS, token/sec, p95/p99), cost projection sheet, recommended reserved+burst configuration, migration checklist for production cutover.

Stitch-ins (artifacts): pricing deck link and sizing workbook shared (linked_drive_docs). Internal SE note: follow up with microbenchmarks asap and lock POC start window.

Notes style: shorthand/CRM-style fragments common — include direct quote from CTO in workshop: "We need predictable throughput during open-house weekends — losing latency there costs us customers."
